answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a scarce, non-transferable credential earned through verifiable work before it can transact. Think of it like a lagoon with a single narrow channel: many boats may drift in, but only those carrying a basalt ballast stone, proof of real effort, pass through. Reputation then accumulates like light from a lantern, visible to everyone, hard to fake, and dimmed instantly when an agent misbehaves, so creating a hundred fake identities costs far more than it earns.
